options: A US aid program for Western European economic recovery after WWII
A US plan to dismantle German industry and divide it among the Allies
A Soviet-led program to rebuild factories across the Eastern Bloc
A NATO military alliance to contain communism across Western Europe
questions.explain: It transferred billions in aid to European countries to rebuild economies after the war.

questions.q: Which country received the largest share of Marshall Plan money?
options: Western Germany
The United Kingdom
The Netherlands
Metropolitan France
questions.explain: The UK received about 26%, followed by France 18% and West Germany 11%.

questions.q: What did the Soviet Union do with the aid offer?
options: Asked for it to be paid as loans instead of grants
Refused it and blocked Eastern Bloc countries from it
Accepted a reduced amount and shared it with Poland
Accepted it only for East Germany and Czechoslovakia
questions.explain: The USSR refused and blocked benefits to Eastern Bloc countries like Romania and Poland.

questions.q: By how much was output in 1951 higher than 1938 for all recipients?
options: At least 35%
About 3%
At least 83%
Half a percent
questions.explain: Output in 1951 was at least 35% higher than in 1938.

questions.q: What does the passage suggest about the plan's effect on recovery?
options: It was the sole cause of growth, as aid exceeded a third of national income
Its contribution is debated, as aid was only about 3% of national income
It had little effect because output stayed below 1938 levels through 1951
It mostly harmed Europe by adding debt equal to 30% of national income
questions.explain: Aid was about 3% of income, and economists are not sure how much growth was due to the ERP.
